answer: Only a random sample of each identity's work is re-executed, but the sampling rate rises for clustered pearl accounts, and a single failed check escalates the whole cluster to full nebula review. Findings land in the tundra record and slash the cluster's shared deposit. Because escalation is public and cheap to trigger, a farm cannot average bad work across many seats the way it can under independent random checks. Every extra seat has to be paid for in work, capital, or time, and none of those can be conjured by a loop.
